subject: Proposed PIP initiation for Rachael Holt — HR/legal check
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed PIP initiation for Rachael Holt — need HR & legal check

Hi Neha & Vivek,

I need to start a confidential coordination thread about Rachael Holt (ENG). Over the last 6 months we've had repeated missed deliverables and several quality regressions on the Search project. I attached a short performance log that highlights the main incidents (missed releases, failure to respond to on-call pages, quality rollbacks). My draft PIP is attached as PIP_draft_v1.docx — it's intentionally conservative (45 days) but I wanted HR and legal input before I share anything with Rachael.

Quick asks:
- HR: does PIP_draft_v1 align with our standard HR language and accommodation processes? Is 45 days appropriate or should we use 60?
- Legal: are there any red flags in the draft re: termination language, progressive discipline, or protected activity?
- Vivek: if we proceed, I plan a one-on-one meeting + formal PIP conversation the week of Mar 22. Can you confirm availability and that you’ll co-lead the meeting?

Confidentiality: please do not include anyone outside this thread (and not Rachael). Im keeping the details minimal in case this is escalated.

Attachments: PIP_draft_v1.docx (draft), performance_log_Mar2026.xlsx (event timeline)

Thanks,

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Product
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Amanda Sullivan <amanda.sullivan@advisoryhr.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed PIP initiation for Rachael Holt — need HR & legal check

Laura / Vivek,

Thanks for pulling this together and for the concise timeline. I reviewed the log and draft; high-level guidance below and I attached an updated PIP template with our recommended wording (PIP_template_v2.docx) plus the HR checklist.

HR recommendations (initial):
- Standardize to a 60-day PIP for performance issues that include code quality + reliability. Gives a clear two-week review cadence (Day 14, Day 30, Day 60).
- Add an accommodations paragraph referencing ADA/leave (we can add boilerplate) and note that PIP is not punitive in itself but a performance-improvement tool.
- Document the prior coaching attempts explicitly in the PIP (you have a few notes in the log; please add meeting dates).
- Evidence: preserve commits, PR reviews, on-call records, and the attached performance log (we will keep in HR file).

Next steps:
1) I will start a private HR file and intake.
2) Amanda (copied) from AdvisoryHR can consult if we want an external neutral facilitator — Amanda, can you confirm availability for a 30-min call this week?
3) We should send this to legal for quick redline before any meeting invite goes to the employee.

Attachments: PIP_template_v2.docx (redrafted), HR_checklist.pdf

If you want, we can hop on a quick call (30m) today at 4pm PT to finalize language.

Thanks,

--
Neha Kapoor
People Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Eden Legal <eden.legal@counselfirm.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Amanda Sullivan <amanda.sullivan@advisoryhr.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed PIP initiation for Rachael Holt — legal input & redline

Neha / Laura / Vivek / Amanda,

Thanks for the context. I reviewed PIP_draft_v1 and the PIP_template_v2 you circulated. High-level legal guidance below; attached are redlines and a short memo.

Legal highlights / recommended edits:
1) Termination & Removal: remove any implied automatic termination language. Ensure that the PIP states performance failure after the PIP may lead to further action up to termination, subject to review.
2) Protected Activity: add a explicit sentence inviting the employee to raise any concerns (harassment, accommodation) and note reasonable accommodations will be considered. This reduces risk around retaliation claims.
3) Evidence & Documentation: be precise about the evidence to be relied on (link to commit hashes/PR IDs and on-call logs). Keep HR's evidence file separate and note the time-window for evidence collection.
4) Consistency: confirm that other employees with similar performance issues received the same cadence (we can review prior cases if needed).
5) Union/Local law: if the employee is in EU/UK, there are extra notice/consultation steps; please tell me Rachaels jurisdiction.

Ive attached: PIP_template_redline.docx and legal_notes.pdf. Suggested timeline: convert to a 60-day plan with checkpoint meetings at Day 14/30/60. If you want, I can prepare a final redline that incorporates Amandas HR language and our legal edits.

DocuSign: I can prepare a signature-ready packet/acknowledgement if you prefer that route.

Regards,

--
Eden Legal (Counsel Firm LLP)
employment@counselfirm.com
eden.legal@counselfirm.com
Attachment: PIP_template_redline.docx (redline), legal_notes.pdf

Markus / Vivek / Neha,

Thanks to Neha, Amanda, and Eden for the quick turnaround. Summary & proposal below: 

Summary of agreed changes:
- Use the HR-approved 60-day PIP template (Nehas PIP_template_v2 as baseline) with Edens redline edits incorporated (no automatic-termination wording; protected-activity language added).
- Checkpoints at Day 14, Day 30, Day 60.
- Evidence bundle: performance_log_Mar2026.xlsx, commit/PR list (I'll export), on-call incident notes (attached to HR file).
- Neha will keep the HR file and coordinate any accommodation requests.

Request for approval: Markus, as VP I need your OK to proceed with a formal meeting and to issue the PIP to Rachael. If you approve, Vivek and I will book the one-on-one + PIP conversation week of Mar 22 (30-min private meeting, 60-min formal PIP conversation).

Please reply with either:
- "APPROVED to proceed" (I'll move forward and send the invite and final doc), or
- "Need more info" (state your blocker).

For transparency, quoting Eden's key advice below:

> "Ensure that the PIP states performance failure after the PIP may lead to further action up to termination, subject to review. Add explicit sentence inviting the employee to raise any concerns (harassment, accommodation) and note reasonable accommodations will be considered."

Attachments: PIP_template_redline.docx, performance_log_Mar2026.xlsx

Confidential reminder: please keep this thread internal.

Thanks,
